from: September book, night 16 (The Mountain of the Lord)
p1: Isaiah lived long ago in Jerusalem. The Lord showed him the last days, before Jesus comes again.
Isaiah saw the Lord’s holy house, the temple, standing on top of the mountains. It stood higher than all the hills.
Why up high? Long ago, people often climbed mountains to be near the Lord.
p2: Isaiah saw people from every land coming to it. They called, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord! He will teach us His ways, and we will walk in His paths.” Today there are temples all over the world!
Tonight, picture a temple shining on a hill. You can walk on the Lord’s path too. Jesus will teach you His ways.
old: Isaiah shared a happy message about a special place: Heavenly Father’s holy house, the temple.
“In the last days,” Isaiah said, “Heavenly Father’s house will stand up high on a mountain, and people from everywhere will want to go there!”
“Come,” the people will say to each other. “Let’s go up to Heavenly Father’s house! He will teach us His good ways, and we will walk in His paths.”
The temple is a peaceful, holy place where we feel very close to Heavenly Father. It’s like His special home, full of light and quiet love.
We can love going to Heavenly Father’s house too. Whether it’s the temple or church, it’s a wonderful place to feel Him near and learn His gentle ways.
